left_defects.source: Pre aute urbes qtidie viribz nroz socoz auget
left_defects.translation: The strength of our allies increases daily before the cities

right_defects.source: Pre aute urbes qtidie viribz nroz socoz auget
right_defects.translation: the city grows daily with the strength of our allies

why: Both split the crossing sentence identically and share the imparatus error; remaining differences are minor and balanced.

left_defects.translation: except the hope of winds for the sails
it might be handled by you

left_defects.source: nisi rones suas ... in alia regione tuta contulerint
left_defects.translation: as many have betaken their own resources to the beginnings of new things in another region

right_defects.source: Aiebat autem rege ipsum nihil tale suspicate
right_defects.translation: The king himself, however, was saying that he had suspected nothing

why: Left garbles the winds-at-the-stern clause just before the break and the safe-transfer clause after it; right errs only on the subject of aiebat.
Both carry que supra | mundum sunt across the break faithfully with no differing defects.

left_defects.source: Wer Abel / Seth / Enoch und Noah? Wer waren die Erzvaeter?
left_defects.translation: Were Abel, Seth, Enoch, and Noah, who were the patriarchs?

why: Left fuses the two questions before the break into a wrong statement; right is faithful though its rendered running head interrupts the crossing sentence.

right_defects.source: vel omnipotentiam Dei recipit ... ut praeclare definiuit concilium Chalcedonense
right_defects.translation: (entire passage after the break omitted; jumps to Pag. 29)

why: Right drops the whole post-break passage including the completion of the crossing sentence.

left_defects.translation: You have valued your own opinion so much that there is none higher
I love men so that they may be pleased

right_defects.source: ut rerum oium ita consiliorum magnam in nos societatem
right_defects.translation: a great partnership of advice toward each other, just as the king of all

why: Right continues the ut-clause across the break (that you trust the old friend) and has fewer mistranslations around it.

left_defects.source: nisi divino munere nra illa nauis ... portum subiisset
left_defects.translation: nor was it by divine favor that that ship of ours ... reached the port unharmed
page-two content of the reply letter rendered before the break, displacing the break

why: Right places gratiam tibi | habuissem correctly at the break and renders nisi divino munere correctly; left misplaces the break and inverts the divine-favor clause.

left_defects.translation: from the poverty of my meager knowledge

why: Both handle recipe | reculabant identically; each has one trivial slip.
Both render the catchword An and the following An the same way with no differing defects.
Both carry attollite | triumphatori dicite across the break faithfully.

right_defects.source: In dnam confido propter dulcedinem nominis sui. Oculi eius
right_defects.translation: In you, Lady, I trust because of the sweetness of your name. Your eyes

why: Right turns the third-person antiphon after the break into second person.
